main_text.p: tis potentia. Aliud demum nascitur dubiū: quomodo uidelicet id fiat, ut idem sit agęs & patiens, quū nihil à se ipso patiatur, sed semper ab alio quod contrarium sit. Propterea Aristoteles libro, de Generatione animalium primo, rectè uidetur negare fe-Cap.20.men esse materiale principium, ubi ipsum coagulo comparat. Quibus in generibus (inquit) mas & fœmina distinguuntur, mas præbet formam & agens est principium, fœmina uero corpus atq; materiam: atque ut in lactis concretione lac ipsum est corpus, coagulum autem densandi cogendiq; principium obtinet. Qua similitudine fe-me, quod coagulo comparat, duntaxat esse agens, & sanguinem maternum, qui uelut lac est, principium passiuum perspicuè demonstrat. At uero Hippocrates & Galenus longè secus existimant. Semen enim nō solummodo esse principium agens, sed etiā patiens profitetur: quorū sententia rationi consentanea est. Nam podagricos, calculosos & epilepticos patres gignere filios his morbis affines & obnoxios, nullis dubium est. Atqui huiusmodi affectus præter naturam à generandi facultate non oriuntur, quia spirituosa duntaxat est, & uitalis calor

page.notes: Running head and page number read from the header; the final digit of 287 is slightly blurred. "dubiū" and "quū" have macrons that are faint on the scan; "nō" and "etiā" likewise. "Quafimilitudine" is printed as one word; given here as "Qua similitudine" with a space, as the sense requires. The bottom-left stain and show-through are not transcribed. The line "feminis," is the catchword, placed under the last line. Printed text is the Latin as copied; no further doubtful readings.
